clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that does MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__, bypassing every subclass constructor entirely — so any current or future MCPError subclass becomes picklable automatically. Its test diff adds `import pickle` and pulls in NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, i.e. it demonstrates the fix on two subclasses with different constructor signatures, not just one. 2555 only adds a __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) is left with the original crash. 2478 adds a similarly-named _restore_mcp_error helper but dispatches per-exc_type (from_error for UrlElicitationRequiredError, from_error_data otherwise), which requires every subclass to expose a compatible reconstructor classmethod; the posted diff also never shows this helper wired into a __reduce__ method or any accompanying test, so it's unclear the pickling path is actually exercised.

clusters.pick_reason: All three stop holding context.lock across the yielded request/response, but #3243 makes a more complete change: it replaces context.lock's type from anyio.Lock to anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), with an inline rationale that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — a pattern anyio.Lock does not support since it enforces same-task release — which #2858 and #3252 do not address (both keep anyio.Lock and only relocate acquire/release points). #3243 also introduces a separate flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions single-flight independently of the general resource-acquisition lock, letting normal concurrent requests proceed unblocked. #2858's given diff is largely unrelated import/docstring cleanup (httpx2->httpx) rather than the lock-scope change itself.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that does MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__, bypassing every subclass constructor entirely — so any current or future MCPError subclass becomes picklable automatically. clusters.pick_reason: All three stop holding context.lock across the yielded request/response, but #3243 makes a more complete change: it replaces context.lock's type from anyio.Lock to anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), with an inline rationale that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — a pattern anyio.Lock does not support since it enforces same-task release — which #2858 and #3252 do not address (both keep anyio.Lock and only relocate acquire/release points). #3243 also introduces a separate flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions single-flight independently of the general resource-acquisition lock, letting normal concurrent requests proceed unblocked. #2858's given diff is largely unrelated import/docstring cleanup (httpx2->httpx) rather than the lock-scope change itself.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 dedups using the existing `str(message.id)` key, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id 1 and string id "1" into the same key (still a latent id-collision bug) and does not guard against a request id literally equal to the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel ("_GET_stream"). #3221 replaces the bare str() cast with a new `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes by type (`i:`/`s:`), closing both edge cases while fixing the same duplicate-in-flight-id race; it's a strict superset fix over #3063's diff in the same function.
